q: Does woodchip or charcoal in a Samalaju ferrosilicon furnace count as zero emissions under CBAM?
title: Biomass reductant in ferrosilicon footprints
short: Ferrosilicon is not a CBAM good, so no CBAM figure is due on it. The question matters for the product footprint EU buyers ask for: woodchip or charcoal carbon counts as biogenic only with evidence of a sustainable source; otherwise count it like coal. Coal, coke and electrode carbon always count.
audience: Ferrosilicon and silicon alloy smelters in Sarawak and their EU buyers

p: Ferrosilicon is declared under CN 7202 21 or 7202 29. The only ferro-alloys in Annex I are ferro-manganese, ferro-chromium and ferro-nickel, so an EU importer of ferrosilicon files no CBAM figure for it. Check Annex I again before each contract season, as the scope can be amended.

EU steel, foundry and silicone customers count purchased ferrosilicon in their Scope 3 and ask for a footprint per tonne. Direct emissions come from the carbon in reductants and electrodes, worked out by mass balance; electricity from the grid sits alongside as Scope 2.

ul: The source of the woodchips or charcoal: plantation, sawmill residue or other.
Certification or a documented chain of custody.
Quantities and carbon content for each delivery.

p: Count the biomass carbon as fossil. Claiming biomass without records is a common reason for a buyer or verifier to reject a footprint.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas and electricity invoices and production records into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so the direct emissions behind each tonne can be traced to the documents. Emissions factors outside India are entered from the official source and labelled.
